This feature disables the accessibility service automatically as soon as any protected app starts — before it reads its state — so banking apps open without crashing (e.g. InstaPay) without opening them via Lord.

Warning: it polls usage events periodically, which consumes battery. When disabled, you can still open a protected app via “Open App via Lord”.

Enable it only if you open banking apps frequently directly from their icons.

On Android 12 and later, the caller number is only delivered to apps that hold call log permission; without it the caller name is never announced even if saved in your contacts, and only what the phone notification shows is spoken. This app is made for blind and low-vision users: granting the log lets it announce the caller by voice before answering, so a blind user knows who is calling before lifting the phone. The permission is used for announcing the name only; nothing else is read.

Some manufacturers pause background voice announcements to save battery. Grant Lord TTS an exemption from battery optimization and open the app settings to confirm background announcements keep working.
Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO device: Lord TTS needs a battery optimization exemption and "Autostart" enabled under Mi security management to keep background voice announcements alive.
Huawei/Honor device: enable the battery exemption and "Auto-launch" under System Manager (Apps > Special) so background voice announcements keep working.
Oppo/OnePlus/realme device: open the battery exemption and allow Lord TTS under "Startup management" in the security center to keep background announcements alive.
Vivo device: enable the battery exemption and "Auto start" under the permission manager so background voice announcements keep working.
Samsung device: enable the battery exemption, open the app settings, and keep Lord TTS out of "Sleeping apps" so background voice announcements keep working.

• Accessibility performance: cache foreground package resolution and sender hint, pass maxNodes/maxTimeoutMs bounds in SafeNodeWalker, and skip AccessibilityBridge calls when app profiles and contact voices features are off, with guard tests.• Comprehensive fixes for screen services, keyboard, battery, OTP verification, and currency speech (Round 4, items 1 to 24): - Accessibility & Screen Services: combined independent element states in \"Where Am I\" without dropping disabled state on checked/selected nodes; centrally guarded READ_SCREEN and READ_CLIPBOARD by their respective feature flags; fixed full URL reading path to bypass shortening and duplicate \"link\" prefixes; cancelled scheduled resume alarm on manual pause switch while guarding resume receiver by pause generation; enabled TOGGLE_PAUSE shortcut to resume screen services while keeping other commands suppressed when paused. - Keyboard & Typing Echo: corrected CommitGate to allow rapid re-entry of the same key in new touch cycles while suppressing duplicate events within the same cycle; preserved prior letter layer upon entering symbols to restore Arabic or English correctly; disambiguated URI fields from numeric passwords to ensure proper key confirmation echo; safe deletion of selected text and multi-byte emojis without UTF-16 surrogate corruption; scaled keyboard and row heights proportionally to size preference and available space. - Bluetooth & Battery: registered Bluetooth receiver with RECEIVER_EXPORTED on API 33+ for Bluetooth permission broadcasts; debounced Bluetooth status churn via safely coalesced delays; avoided leaving % placeholder in charger announcements when sticky broadcast is absent; uncoupled charger connect/disconnect from 100% full battery announcement; strictly respected sound-effect-only battery mode without falling back to speech; bound full battery announcement to foreground service lifecycle and guarded disabled battery levels. - Spoken OTP & Currencies: redacted OTP codes and sensitive text from repeat speech history; bounded OTP pattern matching to prevent truncating longer digits; supported hyphen/space-separated OTP codes and unified normalization for Eastern and Persian numerals while excluding dates/phone numbers; maintained large number precision in currency converter without Long overflow or Double roundoff; rounded currency fractions half-up; separated negative signs cleanly for negative amounts and zero. • Comprehensive fixes for text/number transform, audio streaming, gestures, chat summaries, contact voices, and cross-process storage sync (Orders 1 to 6, Items 1-29): - Text & Numbers: Multi-segment version speech (e.g. 1.6.164, 10.20.300) without breaking decimals, thousand separators, or IP addresses; strict time pattern boundaries avoiding sub-matches in longer tokens; seconds support in 12/24h formats; rigorous leap year and calendar date validation; accurate Roman numeral parsing; and precise bit/byte unit distinction. - Audio Streaming: Decoupled transfer chunk boundaries from actual audio segments in ChunkCrossfader and NateqTtsService eliminating sample loss, and seamless phase-continuous audio resampling in PcmResampler. - Keys & Typing Echo: Reliable double/triple volume key gesture discrimination in ShortcutGestureDetector without spurious cancellation; single long-press trigger; robust KeyShortcutRouter and CallKeyDetector; and privacy-aware typing echo filtering. - Chat Summaries & Readers: Stable conversation identifiers in ChatSummaryHandler preventing cross-chat fingerprint mixing; correct seen/commit ordering; deduplication in ChatLiveReader; and atomic pronunciation dictionary transactions, export, and import. - Contact Voices: Strict suffix matching in ContactVoiceLookup restricted to valid phone numbers without name distortion; safe cross-process index synchronization in ContactVoiceStore; and stable LordPhoneActivity and CallRecordManager handling. - Storage Sync, Features & Backup: Cross-process UnlabeledElementStore synchronization with focus snapshot TTL and self-exclusion; milestone and regression progress monitoring; smart pause for calls and games with manual pause precedence; full backup/restore for Speed Dial and custom element labels; and resilient DownloadHttpHelper 206 resume with clean fallback. • Comprehensive Nateq fixes for voice import safety, engine readiness, Read Later durability, speed metric honesty, and support relay delivery: - Voice Import Safety: Pre-verification in staging for Acapela and Vocalizer packages, ini files, and hdrs; atomic copy with instant rollback journal on failure without touching live data. - Engine Readiness: Cross-process readiness registry (HostWarmStatusRegistry) tracking warmth over IPC without false caches; resolved single-flight race via CompletableDeferred; service generation and speech flag tracking during settings updates; preserved Microsoft session and models with native SSML cleanup. - Read Later & Backup: Atomic full-text persistence in dedicated files without blocking main thread, orphaned file cleanup, 10MB backup/restore expansion, and explicit null representation across IPC in SettingsAuthority and SnapshotPrefs. - Speed Metric Honesty: Excluded unmeasured values (-1) from average, median, and p95 in UnifiedSpeechTracker and SalmaSpeechTracker; restricted firstTrackWrite to actual AudioTrack writes; request correlation tracking with finally block error/cancellation capture. - Support Relay Worker: Explicit processing states (processing, delivered, failed_permanent), bounded retries (5) for transient errors, multipart partial delivery tracking, and strict media and document delivery verification before confirming success. • Unified first-speech latency optimization across all embedded engines (Vocalizer, Acapela, and Microsoft): introduced VoiceReadinessCoordinator preparing active voices on IO with immediate cancellation when speech arrives, reused warm SpeechSynthesizer sessions, licenses, and ONNX models in MicrosoftHostSession (saving >1s per phrase), retained warm Vocalizer voices, eliminated main-thread disk I/O in UI via in-memory repositories (VocalizerVoiceRepository and MicrosoftVoiceRepository), and added comprehensive cross-engine latency tracking and performance counters (UnifiedSpeechTracker and EnginePerformanceCounters). • Fix Nateq responsiveness and Salma speech startup latency: removed repeated logcat process executions from the hot speech path in AcapelaHostSession (saving 300–600ms per utterance), eliminated synchronous main-thread disk inventory and stat checks in the UI in favor of memory snapshots with shared background refreshes, accurately tracked end-to-end Salma speech latency via SalmaSpeechTracker measuring TTFB across all utterances without omission (distinguishing raw PCM, track write, and playback head start), and instrumented thread-safe AcapelaPerformanceCounters to guarantee zero scans, config reads, full hashes, and re-inits on the warm path. • Acapela main-thread performance optimization and AppIntegrity hook detection overhaul: introduced immutable in-memory snapshot repository (AcapelaVoiceRepository) serving settings UI, status summaries, and voice catalogs on main thread with zero disk I/O, coalesced concurrent requests with IO-only discovery, keyed resolver and verification caches by real installation revision across processes without recursive tree walking, reused warm verification results during speech eliminating heavy full-file SHA-256 reads, replaced over-broad substring matching (hook/sandbox/virtual) in AppIntegrity with parsed /proc/self/maps module basename inspection for confirmed Frida/Xposed modules and classified ambiguous indicators as non-blocking diagnostic suspicion preventing false positives on Android 14, and structured diagnostics with rate-limited, legible properties without double negatives. • Fixed release readiness checking in UpdateChecker and hardened release script: distinguished releases in preparation (ReleaseNotReady) due to missing or starter assets from architectural incompatibility (NoCompatibleVersion), prevented caching negative/in-progress states with unconditional cache bypass on manual check, and hardened the release script (scripts/release.ps1) with proactive APK structure and JNI verification, draft release staging, and mandatory pre-publication SHA-256 validation. • Fixed caller announcement with screen locked and normalized caller numbers: Applies best-effort Arabic processing (common Egyptian substitutions and light tashkeel for selected words; 70 dictionary entries: 40 Egyptian replacements + 30 light-tashkeel words) before sending to any engine, independently of tashkeel preservation. Tashkeel is added only for engines that pronounce it correctly (e.g. Google) and skipped for built-in Vocalizer, Microsoft, or unknown engines.
